defect.evidence_quote: The fact that the police misrepresented the statements that Rawls had made is, while relevant, insufficient in our view to make this otherwise voluntary confession inadmissible.
defect.problem: The core holding is supported, but the holding field ends with an unfinished 'deception…' fragment and should state the totality/factor caveat expressly.
defect.proposed_fix: Police misrepresentation that Rawls had confessed was relevant but insufficient to make an otherwise voluntary confession inadmissible; voluntariness turns on the totality of the circumstances.

reasons: The opinion states the officer falsely told petitioner that Rawls had confessed before petitioner gave the confession.
The opinion rejected the involuntariness challenge after noting partial warnings, short duration, normal maturity/intelligence, and the totality of the circumstances.
residual_risks: The case does not support a categorical rule that all police deception is permissible; it supports a totality-based conclusion on these facts.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace the fragmentary holding with a complete sentence tying deception to the totality-of-the-circumstances analysis.
